beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit credentials into repo or logs, and provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead of real secrets.

Create and reuse a single long-lived MongoDB/MongoClient instance per process (do not create a new client per request); configure connection pool size (maxPoolSize) appropriate to expected concurrency.
Enable TLS/SSL for client connections and restrict cluster network access using IP firewall rules or VNet/private endpoints so only the app and operator IPs can reach the cluster.

Do not store or transmit raw client PII or full portfolio documents to third-party LLMs unless you have explicit consent and a documented data handling policy; redact or minimize sensitive fields before sending.

Keep vector embeddings in a dedicated collection (e.g., research_documents) and keep metadata fields used for filtering (client_segment, product, date) as separate indexed scalar fields to enable efficient hybrid filtering.
Create an ascending index on client_id (and on any scalar filter fields used by the agent) to make portfolio document lookups and filtered vector retrievals fast (e.g., {client_id: 1}).

When creating vector indexes, specify index params (index type HNSW or DiskANN, and tuning params like 'm', 'efConstruction' or 'efSearch') appropriate to target latency/recall and test performance with representative queries.

Normalize and store embeddings as fixed-size float arrays (consistent dimension, e.g., 1536), and record the embedding model and dimension in collection metadata so reindexing is possible when the model changes.
Limit returned fields (projections) to just what's needed for the agent (id, snippet, metadata) when retrieving documents to reduce network transfer and memory use during RAG assembly.

Implement transient error handling with exponential backoff and jitter when calling the DB and the LLM; treat network, timeout and server selection errors as retryable and bound retries to a safe max.

Enable server-side retryWrites and configure the driver to use sensible serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS to avoid long request hangs; handle DuplicateKey and idempotency explicitly for write retries.

Use writeConcern 'majority' (or the equivalent durable write setting) for portfolio upserts when the application requires read-after-write consistency, or explicitly read with majority readConcern after a critical write.

Use small, focused transactions only when you must update multiple documents atomically (e.g., portfolio + audit record); otherwise prefer single-document atomic operations to avoid transaction overhead.

Keep a separate collection for client portfolios (portfolio documents) and avoid embedding large blobs; store references to research doc IDs and materialized small summaries for quick agent context assembly.

Provision cluster compute and index memory to match vector index requirements—HNSW/IVF/DiskANN need significant RAM/disk; test index creation on staging and measure memory and disk growth during seeding.

When doing hybrid retrieval (filter by client attributes then vector search), apply the scalar filter first to narrow candidate set; if DB supports hybrid vector+filter index, prefer that to post-filtering for performance.

Use unit and integration tests that can be toggled to run against the live cluster via an env flag; tests must clean up created test data (use a dedicated database sample_banking_10) and avoid mutating other databases.

Instrument and export key metrics and slow query logs (index builds, vector query latencies, connection pool usage, disk usage) to a monitoring system and alert on high error rates or resource saturation.

Avoid sending entire portfolio docs to the LLM when a short structured context or a small extracted summary suffices; implement a context engineer step that trims portfolio context to tokens budget and preserves necessary facts.

Use an external secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) for production credentials and rotate credentials regularly; if Azure AD/MManaged Identity is supported for Mongo API, prefer it over static passwords.
